summary: With a Claude plan on your own computer, stay on Claude. Fable, Opus and Sonnet each passed all eleven checks in under five minutes and spent no credits.

For a shared studio, where the plan is not allowed, Claude Sonnet 5.5 through OpenRouter is the default to pick. All eleven checks in 75 seconds for $0.27: the fastest run of all, and a quarter of what GPT 6.2 Sol cost for the same result in 10.6 minutes.
Cheap models are good enough for this kind of job. Claude Haiku 5.5 ($0.04), GLM 5.3 Flash ($0.05) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ($0.07) each built a correct, working dashboard.

Paying more did not buy more correctness. The three dearest runs (Kimi K3.1 Pro $2.00, GPT 6.2 Astra $1.96, Grok 4.7 $1.96) were no more correct than the cheapest. Astra's table does not sort, and Grok was still working when the 15-minute limit stopped it.
Four built nothing: Kimi K2.7 Code said it was done after loading two skills, and Mistral Large 4.0, Hunyuan HY4 and MiMo V2.6 Pro had built nothing after 15 minutes.

The studio's own instructions and tools carry most of the result: the same checks pass across families and the pages share a house style. What differs between models is speed, cost and how far they push the design.

picks.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
picks.why: Through OpenRouter: every check passed in 75 seconds for $0.27. Nothing else was both this fast and this cheap at this level.

picks.name: Claude Fable 5.2
picks.why: Puts the three findings directly under the headline numbers as big figures, with the leaderboard beside the chart. The clearest layout of information, in one reading of the pictures.

picks.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
picks.why: $0.04 and 2.7 minutes through OpenRouter. GLM 5.3 Flash ($0.05, 2.0 minutes) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ($0.07) are the alternatives outside Anthropic.

picks.name: GPT 6.2 Sol
picks.why: A hero banner, section navigation and icon tiles: it looks most like a product. It took 10.6 minutes and $1.00, and its provider rate-limited it twice earlier that day.

picks.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
picks.why: $0.75, 5 minutes, every check, and its chart titles state the finding instead of naming the axis.

notes.plan/fable: Navy header band; the three findings sit right under the headline numbers as large figures, and the leaderboard is beside the monthly chart. The clearest layout of the lot.
notes.plan/opus: Warm cream page with orange bars; dense and tidy, cities and channels side by side with paired revenue and win-rate bars.
notes.plan/sonnet: The same warm palette as Opus with a larger, labelled monthly chart. Plain and clear.
notes.anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5: Close to the plan run's page: clean, restrained, nothing wasted.
notes.anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5: Teal bars with a value on every month, section links under the title. Simple and readable; nothing looks cheap about it.
notes.openai/gpt-6.2-sol: The most ambitious design: a green hero banner with an illustration, tabs, icons on each tile, findings beside the chart.
notes.openai/gpt-6.2-astra: Polished: dark header, a highlighted revenue tile, findings beside the chart. But clicking a column heading does not reorder the orders table, which shows five rows a page.
notes.openai/gpt-6.1-terra: Calm green page with its own navigation and a 'Sales overview' title. Restrained and professional.
notes.google/gemini-4-neon: Findings first, each as a labelled card with its number; standard blue charts below. Compact.
notes.google/gemini-4-hydrogen: Findings up top, and each chart's title says what it shows ('Won revenue peaked in April…'). Good at telling you what to look at.
notes.google/gemini-4-carbon: Much like Hydrogen's page, findings first. It was still checking its work when the limit stopped it.
notes.moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro: An editorial headline ('The year in solar sales.'), its own navigation and an insight panel beside the chart. Distinctive, and the dearest run here.
notes.moonshotai/kimi-k3: Compact and plain; abbreviates the revenue tile to $4.11M with the full figure beneath.
notes.deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash: The studio's default look, with section links and a long, complete page. Competent rather than designed.
notes.deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017: A warm gradient header and a sentence that frames the year before the numbers. A step up in looks from the other Flash.
notes.deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813: Clean default blue. It could not see its own page (text only), and it shows no sign of that.
notes.z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx: Plain and text-heavy near the top, with an explanation of each formula. Correct, not pretty.
notes.z-ai/glm-5.3-flash: Orange accent and the findings above the chart. A lot of page for five cents.
notes.z-ai/glm-5.3: Filter chips instead of drop-downs, clean blue charts. Also text only, also fine.
notes.x-ai/grok-4.7: A plain blue page that opens with a sentence summing up the year. Complete when it was stopped.
notes.x-ai/grok-build-0.1: The plainest: stock chart styling in cyan, and its city and channel charts put revenue and win rate on two different scales, which is hard to read.
notes.minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash: A report-style headline ('How Brightline Solar sold solar in 2025') in a narrow column. Complete when it was stopped.
notes.minimax/minimax-m3: Peach background with orange bars; simple and warm.
notes.stepfun/step-5-preview: Clean, with a light and dark switch of its own. It needed 86 model calls and $1.79 to get there.
